metadata.note: Morgan's Louisiana and Texas Railroad and Steamship Company (Charles Morgan's road, 1869-1885) and the Southern Pacific branch service on its lines. Morgan's own-name main line Algiers - Morgan City 1870-1882 and Morgan City - Lafayette 1880-1882 (from 1883 the main line is drawn by data/southern_pacific_sunset_route.geojson); and the branches Alexandria, Thibodaux, Napoleonville, Cypremort, St. Martinville, Arnaudville and Salt Mine, each drawn only for its research report's drawable span.
metadata.ownership_split: Main line: Morgan's L&T to 1882; Southern Pacific from 1883 (existing Sunset Route layer; SP through service from 5 Feb 1883). Branches: split at the SP Company lease of 1 Mar 1885 (CSRM) - Morgan's L&T to 1884, Southern Pacific from 1885 - because an Alexandria timetable card still read 'TIME TABLE MORGAN'S LOUISIANA AND TEXAS' in Jan 1884. Rule 4 split features share identical geometry: mlt-alexandria-branch / sp-mlt-alexandria-branch and mlt-thibodaux-branch / sp-mlt-thibodaux-branch. NOT splits: Charles Morgan individual -> Morgan's L&T RR & SS Co (1 Apr 1878, same name on the trains); T&NO title/lease 1927, merger 1934, SP 1961 (Southern Pacific trains throughout). The Southern Pacific colour is pulled from data/southern_pacific_sunset_route.geojson; Morgan's L&T has its own new colour.
metadata.omitted: Not drawn, per the report's drawable fields: Leonville Branch Arnaudville - Port Barre, Weeks Island extension Cypremort - Weeks Island, Lockport Branch Raceland Jct - Lockport, South Bend Branch Bayou Sale - South Bend (drawable NONE - no confirmable passenger year; not proven freight-only either). Houma Branch Schriever - Houma: the report offers a LOW-confidence 1900 [ANCHOR] resting on one indirect social note ('arrived on Thursday evening's train from Houma', St. Mary Banner 23 Jun 1900) against an 1887 livery ad offering buggy connections to Houma from the main-line train; OMITTED until a timetable is read. Lafayette - Baton Rouge Branch: already drawn as tno-lafayette-baton-rouge in data/ymv_baton_rouge.geojson (not edited here; the report lists a start-year defect there, 1900 drawn vs 1911 proven). Main line from 1883: already drawn by the Southern Pacific Sunset Route layer. Morgan City - Galveston etc. Morgan Line steamships and bayou steamers: water transport. Davids - Milton (Franklin and Abbeville Ry), New Iberia - Abbeville (Iberia and Vermilion), Westwego - Bayou Goula (sold to the New Orleans Pacific 1881): not Morgan's trains. Alexandria Branch trains' run Cheneyville - Alexandria over the Texas and Pacific: not Morgan's track.
metadata.not_yet_sourced: [OPEN] ends (last CONFIRMED year, not a known end): Southern Pacific Alexandria Branch 1911; Thibodaux Branch 1922; Napoleonville Branch 1922 (and its 1909 start - opened 1899, passengers unproven 1899-1908); Cypremort Branch 1951 (and its 1900 start - opened 1884; the 1923-1950 continuity is unchecked); St. Martinville Branch 1904 (and its 1886 start - opened 1882). [ANCHOR] single years: Arnaudville Branch 1899, Salt Mine Branch 1885. Houma Branch omitted: a single low-confidence 1900 sighting, and whether it carried passengers at all in the 1870s-80s is open. Salt Mine Branch in 1951: a headerless Official Guide fragment (OG52 173229-173232) may or may not be an SP mixed. Alexandria Branch 1881 (Lafayette - Washington opened May 1881) has no passenger sighting. Main-line local trains 1883-1884 may still have carried the Morgan's name (the existing SP layer draws them as SP; not asserted as a defect). Every headway and most speeds are estimates. A 1920s-1940s SP Atlantic System public timetable or Louisiana PSC discontinuance orders would settle most branch ends.
metadata.freight_only_check: Every branch ends at its last confirmed passenger year, never at the 1951 freight-only dagger or an abandonment date. No freight-only branch, spur or extension is drawn.
metadata.horsecar_check: None - steam road from the NOO&GW's 1854 opening.

properties.geometry_quality: Real-traced, no straight-line legs. Traced 80.1 mi against 80.6 mi Algiers - Morgan City (Fowler tables 55/56; ICC 'about 80.60 miles'). Miles by source (router, before simplification): {'SP': 76.4, 'trail:Mississippi River Trail': 1.5, 'MP': 1.4, '(untagged)': 1.2, '(connector)': 0.1}. The Algiers end (about 3 mi through Algiers and Gretna) runs over OSM ways tagged MP (Brooklyn Ave razed grade) and the Mississippi River Trail; the Algiers terminal point is placed at the Algiers Point riverfront and is APPROXIMATE - the exact Morgan's depot/ferry slip site (opposite Esplanade/Elysian Fields) was not located. Drawn on the ORIGINAL west-bank alignment Algiers - Gretna - Westwego - Avondale (abandoned SP grade, then the SP Avondale Subdivision), NOT the 1935 Huey P. Long Bridge approach used by the Southern Pacific Sunset Route layer. LATER ALIGNMENT: west of Avondale the line is drawn on the present BNSF Lafayette Subdivision as OSM records it; any realignment since the 1870s (bridges at Des Allemands, Bayou Lafourche, Bayou Boeuf; the 5 ft 6 in gauge era to 1872) was not checked. The Brashear (Morgan City) terminus is drawn at the east-bank town, about 0.5 km short of the Berwick Bay waterfront where the trains met the Morgan Line steamships.

segments.note: Morgan's boat-train era: Algiers (ferry from New Orleans) - Brashear City (renamed Morgan City), connecting at Berwick Bay with the Morgan Line steamships to Galveston, Sabine Pass and Indianola and bayou steamers to Franklin, New Iberia and St. Martinville. Charles Morgan bought the New Orleans, Opelousas and Great Western at foreclosure 31 Jul 1869 (ICC); 1869 is left to the NOO&GW, whose own ads run in Jan and Mar 1869 - first Morgan-name passenger evidence is May 1870 (New Orleans Republican 3 May 1870 p8: 'the arrival of the 8 A.M. trains from Algiers'), and a Jan 1871 ad reads 'BERWICK'S BAY ROUTE VIA MORGAN'S LOUISIANA AND TEXAS RAILROAD'. Charles Morgan owned it individually to 1 Apr 1878, then Morgan's L&T RR & SS Co (ICC) - same name on the trains, not a split. Gauge 5 ft 6 in until 1872 (ICC). Headway 1440 is an ESTIMATE from the 1869-71 ads' one morning train each way; no finer headway is asserted.
sources: Segment-level: start 1870 from New Orleans Republican 3 May 1870 p8 and Planters' Banner 29 Mar 1871 p3 (Morgan-name train ads); ownership dates from the ICC valuation; end 1879 = the year before the Lafayette extension opened (ICC, May 1880).

segments.note: Through-route era under Morgan's own name: from May 1880 the main line ran on west of Morgan City to Lafayette (Vermilionville) - see mlt-morgan-city-lafayette - and through New Orleans - Houston trains ran from 30 Aug 1880 (TSHA). Ends 1882 as a DISPLAY boundary, not an end of service: Southern Pacific Sunset Route through service began 5 Feb 1883 and data/southern_pacific_sunset_route.geojson draws this corridor as Southern Pacific from 1883 (on the later Huey P. Long Bridge approach). Headway 1440 is an ESTIMATE; no finer headway is asserted.
sources: Segment-level: 1880 extension opening from the ICC valuation and St. Landry Democrat 31 Jul 1880 p4; 1883 SP through-service boundary from TSHA and the existing Sunset Route layer.

segments.note: Southern Pacific (Atlantic System) under the 1 Mar 1885 lease of Morgan's L&T (CSRM); the 1885 start is an ownership boundary inside a span confirmed at 1884 and 1911, not a fresh opening. Continuity rests on sightings at both ends: Grand Coteau in the 1884 Official Guide (Fowler 'q'), Willow Glen 1909w(fstop) (Fowler), and the Lafayette Advertiser station card of 14 and 21 Feb 1911 ('Alexandria Branch. No. 706, 10:40 a.m. ... No. 705 ... 1:45 p.m.'). [OPEN] Passenger service confirmed to 1911. This is the last CONFIRMED year, NOT a known end - no source dates when passenger service actually stopped (the stations are daggered freight-only by the 1951 Official Guide index). Do not extend without evidence. By 1951 Carencro, Sunset and Cheneyville are daggered and the Guide prints a 'Freight Service only' table Lafayette - Opelousas - Washington. Service surely ran past 1911 (Fowler cites a 1927 company timetable for nearby SP branches) but no later timetable was read. Title passed to the Texas and New Orleans 1927 (CSRM) - still Southern Pacific trains, not a split. Headway 1440 is an ESTIMATE (one or two round trips a day on branches in the schedules read).
sources: Segment-level: 1885 lease from the CSRM finding aid; continuity and the 1911 last-confirmed year from Fowler 65 dated sightings and Lafayette Advertiser 14 Feb 1911 p3; freight-only by 1951 from the Official Guide index (OG52).

segments.note: Southern Pacific (Atlantic System) under the 1 Mar 1885 lease of Morgan's L&T (CSRM). 1887 'RAILROAD SCHEDULE. THIBODAUX BRANCH': two round trips daily Thibodaux - Schriever, 'connection at Schriever Station with the trains of the Southern Pacific Company, Atlantic System, Morgan line' (Weekly Thibodaux Sentinel 3 Sep 1887). From 1899 every Napoleonville train also ran over this piece. Last CONFIRMED year 1922: train No. 203 was due at Thibodaux at 6 P.M. until 11 Sep 1922, when Nos. 203/204 were discontinued on the PSC petition (filed in the corporate name Morgan's L&T) - the paper calls it a CURTAILMENT, so other trains continued by an unknown amount (Thibodaux Commercial Journal 19 Aug and 23 Sep 1922). [OPEN] Passenger service confirmed to 1922. This is the last CONFIRMED year, NOT a known end - no source dates when passenger service actually stopped (the stations are daggered freight-only by the 1951 Official Guide index). Do not extend without evidence. (Thibodaux is indexed 'Southern Pacific, 56†' in 1951.) TRAP: the Texas and Pacific's own 'Thibodaux Branch' out of Donaldsonville is a different railroad. Headway 720 from the 1887 two round trips a day; ESTIMATE for other years.
sources: Segment-level: 1885 lease from CSRM; 1887 schedule Weekly Thibodaux Sentinel 3 Sep 1887 p1; 1922 last-confirmed year Thibodaux Commercial Journal 19 Aug 1922 p1 and 23 Sep 1922 p3; freight-only by 1951 from the OG52 index.

segments.note: Baldwin - Glencoe - Cypremort, trains running to and from Franklin. Opened August 1884 under Morgan's (ICC; Sugar Bowl via Opelousas Courier 9 Aug 1884), but nothing confirms PASSENGERS 1884-1899, so neither the Morgan's era nor 1885-1899 is drawn. [OPEN] start: first CONFIRMED passenger year 1900 ('Nos. 68 and 69 are the Cypremort Branch trains', St. Mary Banner 17 Mar 1900). Confirmed again 1903 (Nos. 70/71, St. Mary Banner 21 Feb 1903), 1922 (one round trip Franklin - Cypremort, St. Mary Banner 3 and 10 Jun 1922) and 1951 (Official Guide table dated 29 Apr 1951: No. 406 MIXED, Franklin 1:16 PM - Baldwin - F. & A. Junction - Caneland - Glencoe - Cypremort; Cypremort and Glencoe indexed with no dagger). GAP CAVEAT: drawing straight through 1923-1950 rests on sightings at both ends of a single branch with no evidence of a gap - no 1923-1950 timetable was read, and a suspension in those years would not be visible in these sources. [OPEN] Passenger service (a mixed train) confirmed to 1951. This is the last CONFIRMED year, NOT a known end - no source dates when it stopped. Do not extend without evidence. Southern Pacific trains throughout (T&NO title 1927, merger 1934, SP 1961 are not splits). Headway 1440 is an ESTIMATE from the one round trip a day in the 1903 and 1922 schedules.
sources: Segment-level: 1900 from St. Mary Banner 17 Mar 1900 p3; 1903 St. Mary Banner 21 Feb 1903 p3; 1922 St. Mary Banner 10 Jun 1922 p5; 1951 Official Guide (research/sources/official_guide_1952.txt lines 173270-173281 and index).

segments.note: [ANCHOR] Single proven year. St. Martinville Junction - Levert - Parks - Breaux Bridge - Lelia - De Clouet - Arnaudville. Feb 1899: a Mardi Gras 'special train will leave St. Martinville for Breaux Bridge and Arnaudville' and 'Wednesday the train on the branch road commenced to run from Arnaudville to New Iberia' (Weekly Messenger 4 Feb 1899); 'The trains over the branch road to Arnaudville now make New Iberia their terminus instead of Cade Station ... passengers travelling over the Arnaudville road' (New Iberia Enterprise 11 Feb 1899). CONFLICT recorded: the ICC gives 'opened for operation May, 1899'; the newspapers show trains in February. Service certainly ran wider than 1899 both ways (into later years at least), but NO other year is confirmed - do not widen this anchor without a source, and do not delete it. Operator: Southern Pacific (corporate name Morgan's L&T) from opening. By 1951 Breaux Bridge is daggered for SP and Arnaudville is Missouri Pacific only. TRAP: the New Iberia and Northern (MoPac) also served Breaux Bridge and Arnaudville. Headway 1440 is an ESTIMATE.
sources: Segment-level: Weekly Messenger 4 Feb 1899 p3 and New Iberia Enterprise 11 Feb 1899 p3; opening date conflict from the ICC valuation.

segments.note: [ANCHOR] Single proven year. New Iberia - Davids - Iberia & Vermilion Junction - Salt Mine (Avery Island), opened June 1883 under Morgan's (ICC). The only confirmed passenger year: in April 1885 a party of excursionists 'proceeded to the Salt Mines ... The train going out at 7 o'clock and returning at 10 would barely have given them time ... hence ... a request for special hours in the running of the train' (New Iberia Enterprise 4 Apr 1885) - a regular train carrying passengers, in the Southern Pacific lease era (from 1 Mar 1885, CSRM). Service certainly ran wider than 1885 both ways, but NO other year is confirmed - do not widen this anchor, and do not delete it. A headerless 1951 Official Guide fragment with Salt Mine times could not be attributed (see not_yet_sourced). Headway 1440 is an ESTIMATE from the one out-and-back trip the 1885 item describes.
